dimensions.name: Bank size & dedicated volume
dimensions.evidence: The QBank contains 5713 active questions with a high percentage (94.1%) of enriched content. The distribution across subjects is reasonably balanced, with pediatrics, cardiology, and nephrology having substantial representation.
dimensions.gap: While the volume is impressive, the presence of duplicate content and misclassified items suggests a need for better curation.

dimensions.name: NBME blueprint / systems coverage
dimensions.evidence: The QBank covers a wide range of subjects relevant to Step 2, including pediatrics, cardiology, and ob-gyn. However, some subjects like surgery and ethics are underrepresented.
dimensions.gap: Thin coverage in certain areas like surgery and ethics could leave gaps in comprehensive exam preparation.

dimensions.name: Item craft (stem/options/clinical reasoning)
dimensions.evidence: Many items lack a complete vignette, have weak distractors, or are misclassified. This affects the quality of clinical reasoning and decision-making assessment.
dimensions.gap: The absence of well-crafted vignettes and balanced options reduces the effectiveness of the questions in testing clinical reasoning.

dimensions.name: Basic-science ↔ clinical integration (or next-step management for Step 2/3)
dimensions.evidence: Some questions demonstrate integration of clinical scenarios with basic science concepts, but many lack depth and complexity in the vignettes.
dimensions.gap: Improvement is needed in integrating clinical scenarios with underlying mechanisms or management steps to enhance learning.

dimensions.name: Biostats / ethics / CCS readiness (as applicable)
dimensions.evidence: Biostatistics and ethics are present but not robustly covered. The QBank lacks depth in these areas, which are crucial for Step 2/3.
dimensions.gap: A more comprehensive approach to biostatistics and ethics is necessary to ensure readiness for these components of the exam.

dimensions.name: Rationale / teachability (UWorld-depth proxy)
dimensions.evidence: Explanations are often verbose or repetitive, lacking the concise and focused teaching points seen in high-quality resources like UWorld.
dimensions.gap: Explanations need to be more concise and focused on key teaching points to enhance their educational value.

dimensions.name: High-yield disease & pharm readiness
dimensions.evidence: The QBank covers high-yield topics but often lacks depth in pharmacology and disease mechanisms, which are critical for Step 2/3.
dimensions.gap: Greater emphasis on high-yield pharmacology and disease mechanisms is needed to ensure comprehensive exam preparation.

dimensions.name: Quality gates & consistency
dimensions.evidence: Inconsistencies in item classification and the presence of duplicate content indicate a lack of rigorous quality control.
dimensions.gap: Implementing stricter quality control measures could improve consistency and reliability across the QBank.

bank.examTakerVerdict: The QBank offers a substantial volume of questions, but the quality and consistency issues may hinder effective preparation. It is advisable to supplement with other resources for a more comprehensive review.
